Architecture

One audio engine, three thin platform hosts, one session model.

┌──────────────────────────── App (per platform, native UI) ───────────────────────────┐
│  iOS: SwiftUI (touch-first)   Android: Jetpack Compose   macOS: SwiftUI + AppKit      │
│  Library · Decks · Mixer · Workspace layouts · MIDI mapping · Sync client             │
└───────────────▲──────────────────────────────────────────────▲───────────────────────┘
                │ commands (lock-free)                          │ status (atomics, 30–120 Hz)
┌───────────────┴──────────── Platform audio host ─────────────┴───────────────────────┐
│  Route discovery → RoutePlanner → device streams                                      │
│  iOS: AVAudioSession + RemoteIO AUAudioUnit   macOS: Core Audio HAL AUAudioUnit(s)     │
│  Android: AudioManager + Oboe/AAudio stream(s)                                         │
└───────────────▲───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │ sbe.h (C ABI)
┌───────────────┴──────────── Soundboard Engine (C++17, shared) ────────────────────────┐
│  Decks ─► Channel strips ─► Crossfader ─► Master bus ─► Limiter ─► Record tap          │
│                 └─(PFL)──► Cue bus ◄── Preview player                                  │
│                                  └─► Headphone mix (cue/master blend, gain, limiter)  │
│  Router: Master-only · Split-mono · Multichannel · Separate cue device (drift FIFO)   │
│  Sync (tempo + phase PLL) · Transitions · Analysis (BPM/grid, key, loudness, waveform)│
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Engine (engine/)

Signal flow

Deck n ─ trim (+auto-gain) ─ 3-band isolator EQ ─ bipolar filter ─┬─ PFL ─────────────► Cue Σ
                                                                  └─ fader ─ echo ─ xfader ─► Master Σ
Preview player ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────► Cue Σ

Master Σ ─ master gain ─ look-ahead limiter ─┬─ record tap
                                             ├─ (blend) ─► Headphones = Cue Σ·(1−m) + Master·m
                                             └─ latency-compensation delay ─► router
Headphones ─ headphone gain ─ safety limiter ─ latency-compensation delay ─► router
BlockImplementationWhy
Deck playbackCubic Hermite interpolation, variable rate, 4 ms start/stop ramps, 3 ms crossfaded jumpsSeeks, loops, hot cues and stops are click-free (tested: worst step equals the signal's own slope)
EQLinkwitz–Riley 4th-order 3-band isolator, all-pass compensatedFlat (±0.05 dB) at unity, full band kill (−56 dB low, −44 dB high) — club-mixer behaviour
FilterTPT state-variable LP→HP series pairStable under fast sweeps; transparent at centre; no topology switch at zero
CrossfaderConstant-power with curve blend to sharp cutEqual loudness when blending, scratch-cut when wanted; parked side is bit-exact silence
LimiterLook-ahead min-hold + box-average gainMathematically guaranteed ceiling, no instantaneous gain steps
EchoBeat-synced, filtered feedback, post-fader"Echo out" tails survive the fader cut
SyncOne-shot tempo + phase match, then PLL (±1 %)Locks within ~1 s, follows leader tempo changes; half/double-time aware
TransitionsBlend · Bass swap · Filter sweep · Echo out, beat-lengthThe beginner "Mix" button
Drift FIFOSPSC ring + Hermite resampler + PI ratio controlSecond device on its own clock (macOS, Android)

Threading

  • Audio thread calls render()/renderCue(). It never locks, allocates, frees or logs.
  • Control thread calls everything else. Each call becomes a Command on a lock-free SPSC queue, drained at the start of the next callback: changes land on block boundaries, in order.
  • Track memory: the control side owns shared_ptrs; the audio thread sees raw pointers. A generation counter acknowledges swaps so a buffer is only freed after the audio thread has let go.
  • Status: decks and buses publish relaxed atomics after each callback; the UI polls at display rate.

Verified with ThreadSanitizer (400 concurrent load/play/EQ/loop operations against a running audio thread) and AddressSanitizer/UBSan across the full suite.

Output topologies

TopologyDevice viewUsed when
MASTER_ONLYstereo masterNo second path exists — UI explains how to get one
SPLIT_MONOL = master mono, R = cue monoSplitter cable on one stereo jack
MULTICHANNELmaster on pair a, cue on pair b4-ch interface/controller; iOS multi-route aggregate
SEPARATE_CUE_DEVICEmaster device + cue devicemacOS two devices; Android when the policy allows

RoutePlanner (Swift and Kotlin, identical rules, unit-tested on both) picks the topology from the reported outputs, in that preference order, and computes latency alignment.

Analysis (background thread)

  • BPM + beat grid: spectral-flux onset envelope → autocorrelation over a folding range → whole-track comb alignment for sub-0.01 BPM precision → kick-band check to put the grid on the beat, not the off-beat. Tested at 87–140 BPM: exact BPM, grid within ±1 ms.
  • Key: chromagram vs Krumhansl–Kessler profiles; Camelot code and harmonic compatibility.
  • Loudness: ITU-R BS.1770-4 integrated LUFS (reference coefficients reproduced exactly); drives auto-gain so beginners never ride the trim.
  • Waveform: low/mid/high peak bins for the three-colour waveform.

Platform hosts (platforms/)

iOSmacOSAndroid
DiscoveryAVAudioSession.currentRoute, route-change / interruption / media-reset notificationsCore Audio device list, transport type, latencyAudioManager.getDevices, AudioDeviceCallback
OutputRemoteIO AUAudioUnit, N channelsHAL AUAudioUnit per deviceOboe stream(s), LowLatency + Exclusive, index-mask channels
Second path.multiRoute aggregatesecond device + drift FIFOsecond stream, probed, fallback
DecodeAVAudioFileAVAudioFileMediaExtractor + MediaCodec (Phase 1)

Both apps ship a Routing Lab screen: it plays a low pulse on the master and a high chirp on the cue, with meters and the plan explanation, so routing is validated by ear on real hardware before any DJ UI is built on top.

Session model and sync

Local-first, synced when online. Shared schema across platforms (SQLite on every device):

EntityKey fieldsSync rule
Trackcontent hash (first/last 1 MB + duration) + optional audio fingerprintIdentity follows the audio, not the file path
Analysistrack id, grid (bpm, first beat), key, LUFS, waveform blobDeterministic — recomputed locally if missing; manual grid edits win
Cue points / loopstrack id, slot, frame, label, colourPer-field last-writer-wins with hybrid logical clocks
Playlists / cratesordered track idsOperation-based list CRDT (insert/move/remove)
Session / set historyordered entries with timestampsAppend-only
Preferenceskey/valueLWW

CloudKit is not available on Android, so sync is a small service of our own (HTTPS + Postgres, or a hosted CRDT store) with end-to-end encryption of user data. Audio files themselves are not synced by default (licensing and size); the library matches by content hash on each device.

Boundaries and contracts

BoundaryContractRule
App ↔ engineengine/include/soundboard/sbe.h (C ABI)Commands are queued lock-free; status is read from atomics. The app never touches audio buffers
Host ↔ enginesbe_engine_render called from the device callbackThe host owns devices and streams; the engine owns every sample
Engine ↔ analysissbe_track_analyze on a background threadRuns before a track is loaded; results can be cached and re-applied with sbe_track_set_grid and sbe_track_set_auto_gain
Tokens ↔ UIdesign/tokens/obsidian.tokens.jsonGenerated into Swift (and CSS for the site); components use semantic names only

There is no HTTP API, SDK, CLI or MCP server in 0.1.0.

Data model

Everything is JSON in Application Support/Soundboard/ (format and rules in ADR 0007):

FileHoldsShared by
library.jsonTracks (title, artist, duration, location, content hash, analysis, 8 hot cues, saved loop) and playlistsEvery session
sessions/index.jsonNamed sessions and the last one opened—
sessions/<id>.jsonDecks (track, position, tempo, sync, loop, cue, channel strip), master and headphone mixer, queue, library viewOne session
media/<id>.<ext>Audio copied in at import (always on iOS, optional on macOS)Library

Preferences and Appearance are small JSON values in UserDefaults. PCM and waveforms are never stored: a track is decoded when it loads and its waveform drawn from that decode. The session model above is the target for the sync service; the files are its first, local form.

Surfaces

SurfaceWhereFor
Soundboard appplatforms/apple/App, platforms/android (planned)DJs
Routing Labplatforms/apple/RoutingLab, platforms/android/appValidating routing on hardware
Routing prototypeengine/tools/routing_demo.cpp (make demo)Proving master isolation offline
Docs sitepublic/ (generated by tools/site/), root index.htmlPeople and agents; public/llm.txt is the agent entry point

Testing strategy

  • Engine: unit and signal tests in engine/tests/ with synthetic audio (engine/testing/synth.hpp): routing isolation, declick, limiter, drift FIFO, sync, transitions, BPM, key and loudness against known inputs. Run plain and under ASan, UBSan and TSan.
  • Apple: swift test covers token resolution, contrast, generator parity and track matching.
  • Hardware: the on-device matrix in QA; audio behaviour that depends on real devices is never claimed from simulation.
  • Repository: make validate runs every check above plus the Station lint; CI runs the same.

Modules

engine/            C++ core (no platform code): tests, routing prototype
platforms/apple/   SoundboardAudio (session, devices, host, tracks, matching), SoundboardUI
                   (design system, components, screens), Soundboard and Routing Lab apps
platforms/android/ Oboe host (C++/JNI), Kotlin audio layer, Routing Lab
design/tokens/     Obsidian tokens and their generator
tools/             site generator and repository checks
(planned)
shared/schema/     session database schema and migrations (shared SQL)
